actions.heading: Prepare your application and core documents
actions.essential: Prepare the completed amendment application (Form D.R.P/1,7,8), the National Identity card you have been using, a birth certificate or a birth-register extract certified by the Additional District Registrar, and an ICAO-standard photograph taken within the last 6 months. These are the documents everyone needs; the next step covers extra evidence some people must add.

actions.heading: Check whether you need extra evidence
actions.essential: The core documents are enough unless one of these circumstances applies: you have no birth certificate, you were born abroad to a Sri Lankan parent, you hold dual citizenship, you are clergy, or you want to use a husband's name or surname. Each case has its own document, shown on the card with the circumstance it belongs to.

fact.name: Probable age certificate or register search results, with proof of name and date of birth

facts.qualification: Only if you have no birth certificate.

source_context.text: Some applicants must add further evidence: a probable age certificate or register search results with proof of name and date of birth if there is no birth certificate; an affidavit, recognised written evidence and register search results for applicants over 40 with neither; a citizenship certificate for those born abroad to a Sri Lankan parent; a dual citizenship certificate where it applies; clergy documents where they apply; and an attested marriage certificate when using a husband's name or surname.

fact.name: Affidavit, recognised written evidence and register search results (applicants over 40)

facts.qualification: Only for applicants over 40 who have neither a birth certificate nor a probable age certificate.

actions.heading: Divisional Secretary's countersignature
actions.essential: After the Grama Niladhari certifies the application, the Divisional Secretary must countersign it. The countersignature is mandatory for the non-estate route and is in addition to the Grama Niladhari's certification, not a substitute for it.
conditions: The applicant is not an estate resident and seeks an NIC amendment.
actions.explanation_hidden: The countersignature is needed for the application certified by the Grama Niladhari; the estate route does not have this step.
actions.source_wording:
The Divisional Secretary must countersign the application certified by the Grama Niladhari; the countersignature is mandatory.

actions.heading: Have it certified by the Estate Superintendent
actions.essential: Because you live on an estate, forward the application and your documents through the Estate Superintendent, who certifies it. Pay the Rs. 500 amended-card fee through the same certifying officer and keep the receipt, which is one of the documents the department requires. Registered-post delivery under the normal service adds Rs. 120.
conditions: The applicant is an estate resident seeking an NIC amendment.

facts.qualification: Paid through the certifying officer. Registered-post delivery under the normal service adds Rs. 120.

source_context.text: If you live on an estate, forward the application through the Estate Superintendent, who certifies it. Pay the Rs. 500 amended-card fee through the certifying officer and keep the receipt. Registered-post delivery under the normal service adds Rs. 120.

If you do not live on an estate, forward the application through the Grama Niladhari for your area of residence, who certifies it. Pay the Rs. 500 amended-card fee through the certifying officer and keep the receipt. Registered-post delivery under the normal service adds Rs. 120.

actions.heading: Receive your amended card
actions.essential: After certification your application goes to the District Secretariat's ID card division, which forwards it to the Department for Registration of Persons. Under the normal service the amended card is then sent to you by registered post.

If you do not live on an estate, forward the application through the Grama Niladhari for your area of residence, who certifies it. Pay the Rs. 500 amended-card fee through the certifying officer and keep the receipt. Registered-post delivery under the normal service adds Rs. 120.
